Content: Paula discovered `text(three)` sedimentary rock layers that contain fossils of a lizard species. The list below shows how Paula described the lizards' appearance in `text(each layer)`.

Which conclusion do Paula's findings `bbtext(best)` support?

B.Choice: Lizards with long tails lived in the area for a longer period of time.

Content: The list below describes the characteristics of the forelimbs of an American toad and a bottlenose dolphin.

Which conclusion does this information `bbtext(best)` support?

A.Choice: Random chance led to the development of `text(two)` animals with different body structures.

B.Choice: These animals evolved separately from their own unique ancestors and do not share a common ancestor.

C.Choice: These animals share a common ancestor, and natural selection produced `text(two)` animals that use their forelimbs for different purposes.

D.Choice: The toad's ancestors chose to be well-adapted to grasping, while the dolphin's ancestors chose to be well-adapted to moving through water.

Content: Permafrost is created when the water in the ground freezes and remains frozen `text(year-round)`. Alaska has permafrost that has remained frozen for at least `text(12,000 years)`. Scientists have discovered that this permafrost contains powerful greenhouse gases, and the permafrost releases these gases to the atmosphere as it melts. What relationship might exist between global climate change and this permafrost?

B.Choice: Increasing air temperatures will cause less permafrost to melt, and then fewer greenhouse gases will be released into the atmosphere.

C.Choice: The permafrost will cause global air temperatures to decrease, and then more greenhouse gases will get trapped in the permafrost.

D.Choice: The permafrost will cause global air temperatures to increase, and then fewer greenhouse gases will get trapped in the permafrost.

Content: The marine iguana is a swimming lizard that only exists on the Galapagos Islands. A species of land iguana also exists on the Galapagos Islands and other places on `text(Earth)`.
